Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr ¿Stepped¿ pressure build-up tests ¿SPBUT¿ being performed on all (5)wells on the HUNTER pad. The HUNTER 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H wells. These tests are being performed in response to a gas migration investigation in area underway by The Department. SPBUTs were initiated on 5/26/20 @ ~ 08:15 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - All (5) wells on the pad are shut in w/ Frac valves installed on top of well heads. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a temporary poly vent tank via rubber lines. All annuli were closed when I arrived. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Reps. Craig Shores and Trey Sites, Creston Consultant Reps., Tom Messing and Andy Sallaway and D.E.P. OGIS, Ken Kennedy. Starting at approx. 10:15, ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for all the HUNTER Pad wells. - HUNTER 5H: (20x13): 3.0 psi.; 68 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:17 ** (13x9): 277 psi.; 85 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:23 ** (9x5): 327 psi.; 85 % CH4; Sample collected at 10:27 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:20. - HUNTER 6H: (20x13): 17.0 psi.; 65 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:33 ** (13x9): 169.0 psi.; 87 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:37 ** (9x5): 549.0 psi.; 86 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:40 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:40. - HUNTER 22HC: (20x13): 24.0 psi.; 91 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:45 ** (13x9): 226.0 psi.; 89 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:49 ** (9x5): 396.0 psi.; 92 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:52 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:50. - HUNTER 21HC: (20x13): 44.0 psi.; 93 % CH4; Sampled collected @ 10:55 ** (13x9): 268.0 psi.; 90 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:00 ** (9x5): 131.0 psi.; 87 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:07 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 11:00. - HUNTER 23HC: (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0 % CH4; No sample collected (13x9): 255.0 psi.; 89 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:13 (9x5): 321.0 psi.; 86 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:20 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 11:30. - All (5) wells (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened and venting to poly tank @ 11:45. ** The presence of pressure and gas was detected in the (20x13) and the(13x9) annuli of all the wells on the pad with the exception of the HUNTER 23HC (20x13) annulus. This is indicative of defective cement. Since the presence of gas was detected in the HUNTER 5H well (20x13) annulus was not addressed in previous responses received, the Dept. requests in writing, by 7/4/20, how CALLC plans to address this defective condition.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On 11/30/2020, DEP representative John Ciccone completed an administrative inspection report regarding Chesapeake Appalachia LLC's MTL location in response to results for sample ID # 9544-030 becoming available within DEP's Samples Information System (SIS). At the time of this inspection, sample results for sample ID # 9544-030 are in the “In Process” status, with all constituents and parameters being analyzed except for Total Dissolved Solids (TDS).On 10/14/2020, fluid was noted dripping out of a roll-off container stationed on the MTL pad onto the pad surface. Field measured specific conductivity revealed elevated levels of conductivity. One 500mL and one 125mL sample (sample ID # 9544-030) were collected for SAC 942 + Al, Br, Li analysis. Further details regarding the site visit can be found within IR # 3093160.Sample results for sample ID # 9544-030 show the following elevated levels of metals, indicating the release of production and/or flowback fluid:• Manganese – 7.967 mg/L• Barium – 196.7 mg/L• Iron – 31.12 mg/L• Chloride – 4496.7 mg/L• Bromide – 33.98 mg/LBased on these levels, the following violations considered PENDING within IR # 3093160 are now cited against well permit API # 015-23510:• 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)• 25 Pa. Code 78a.66(b)(1)• SWMA 301• CSL 402(b)Please include the required information outlined in 25 Pa. Code 78a.66 as part of the NOV response.The available sample results within SIS for sample ID # 9544-030 have been uploaded to eFACTS with this report.

Comments: On 6/4/19 at 1320 hrs., I conducted an inspection of Alliance Petroleum Co., LLC's J E Walker 3 well (API 063-33366) in East Mahoning Twp., Indiana Co. in response to a complaint filed with the Department on 5/31/19 (CID 342569). The complaint concerned erosion and sedimentation occurring along the access road to the well site. Upon inspection, it was observed that the well pad is permanently stabilized; however, the portion of access road adjacent to the well pad is unstable. In addition, there is accelerated erosion and sedimentation occurring at the lower portion of the access road where it splits off from a shared section of driveway. Additional BMPs are needed to stabilize these sections of the access road. The condition of the access road constitutes violations of 102.4(b)1, 102.22(a), and 78.53. These violations will be resolved upon installation of BMPs needed to stabilize the areas of concern.

Report Details

Permit API: 115-22483
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Apolacon Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-02-06
Comments: The Department, Frank Hoehle, DEP O&G WQS and I arrived at the site at 11:39 to conduct a follow up inspection in reference to a production fluid spill that occurred at the site on 1-6-19. The weather conditions are cloudy skies, breezy, with rainfall approaching, and a temperature of 35 degrees Fahrenheit. For additional details pertaining to the production fluid spill, refer to the Department's 1-6-19, 1-9-19, and 1-17-19 inspection reports, Inspection ID#'s 2831500, 2832214, 2832221. We met with Murray Kush, site company man, completions consultant of Repsol, and Dave Coxhead, Site Safety Man, of REM Security. Deep Well Services Rig # 2 is in the process of drilling out hydraulic fracturing plugs. Mr. Kush informed the Department the following. "The rig is drilling out frac plugs on the 3H well. A total of 22 plugs will be drilled out. We are the 20th plug. The 1H is done. Frac plugs will be drilled out on the 7H next. The working tanks and gas buster tanks near the pad entrance contain fluid from the 3H plug drill outs. Brine was used on the 1H well to drill out the plugs. Fresh water is used to drill out the plugs on the 3H well. Trucks are removing water from 1H plug drill outs, out of the offloading station near the production equipment. Containment is the same since the frac. We added containment under the rig. Gel is used to drill out plug parts." In addition to conducting a follow-up inspection at the site, the Department conducted a review of sample results for a water sample collected at the site on 1-9-19. The PADEP Bureau of Laboratories in Harrisburg, PA forwarded the results to the Department on 2-6-19. On 1-9-19, the Department collected a groundwater sample from the swale at the base of the Caprio Pad where the water exhibited elevated levels conductivity on 1-8-18. The Department identified this water sample as Caprio Pad SW-1. Upon review of the Department's groundwater sample results, it was noted that the sample results had elevated concentrations of barium, lithium, manganese, strontium, aluminum, chloride, and iron. Barium was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential Medium Specific Concentration (MSC) for groundwater of 2,000 micrograms per liter (ug/l) with a concentration of 50,600 ug/l. Lithium was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential MSC for groundwater of 83 ug/l for Residential, Used Aquifers and for Non-residential, Used Aquifers of 230 ug/l with a concentration of 1,270 ug/l. Manganese was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential MSC for groundwater of 300 ug/l with a concentration of 8,000 ug/l. Strontium was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential MSC for groundwater of 4,000 ug/l with a concentration of 38,900 ug/l. Aluminum was detected above the Act 2, Secondary Maximum Contaminant Level (SMCL) of 200 ug/l with a concentration of 41,400 ug/l. Chloride was detected above the Act 2, SMCL of 250,000 ug/l with a concentration of 946,000 ug/l. Iron was detected above the Act 2, SMCL of 300 ug/l with a concentration of 34,400 ug/l. Bromide was detected at a concentration of 7,307.28 ug/l. Calcium was detected at a concentration of 252,000 ug/l. Sodium was detected at a concentration of 389,000 ug/l. Specific See the attached sample results. During the inspection, I utilized a Hanna Groline Soil Test HI 98331 meter, and an Oakton PCTS 50 meter to record specific conductance (conductivity) in water in the sump in the infiltration basin at the toe of fill slope, and in water and damp soil west and slightly up-gradient of the sump, where groundwater seeped to the fill slope. Conductivity readings were in the range of (170-240) microsiemens/cm in the sump, and (700-800) microsiemens/cm in water west of the sump, and (150-200) microsiemens/cm in wet soil west of the sump. See photos. The Department left the site at 12:43.

Comments: On 09/17/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the Harden Farms Well Site following receipt of an incident report that was submitted to the Department on 09/17/2025 at 12:17 (CTS 392314).It was reported that 10 gallons of biocide material was spilled on site at 12:00, 09/17/2025. No waterways were affected. It was also reported that a clean up crew (SPSI) was on site.I called the EQT representative who reported the spill, Lance Witters, for information. I noted that SPSI arrived after I did, and I requested the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) to be sent to me. It was described to me that the material spilled was a Multi-Chem biocide. The cause of the release was that a hose back pressured, biocide flowed back to the tank, and the tank overflowed. It was estimated that 10 gallons spilled.SPSI had not began remediation and was not on the pad when I arrived. No personal were on the pad upon my arrival.The following was observed:The contaminated area was adjacent to the gas production units (GPUs). It was unknown if any production fluid was present in addition to the biocide spilled; no elevated conductivity was observed. No remediation had begun and SPSI was not on the pad when I arrived on the pad. SPSI arrived to the site after the Department (Photo 1). An extremely strong odor was experienced on site in the vicinity of the contaminated area.SPSI then arrived on the pad and had not begun remediation while I was on site. The impacted area was located between the well heads and the GPUs. The impacted area appeared wet with small sections of pooled fluid (Photos 2-5).I asked SPSI if they had the SDS, and they did not. The SDS was not located on site with the site documents in the mailboxes. I was able to locate a Control and Disposal Plan and the Site Specific Safety and Environmental Plan and Policy. I was not able to locate any information related to the Multi-Chem biocide (Photos 6-9). I also did not find a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan (PPC) on site. The SDSs are required to be on site. The PPC Plan is also required to be on site during drilling or completion activities, however the well operator shall prepare and develop a site specific PPC plan prior to storing, using, or generating regulated substances to, on or from a well site.The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance (Photo 10).The Department requests a description of the activities that were being carried out that resulted in a spill.Due to the SDS not present on site, a PPC Plan not on site, failure to control regulated fluids with a release to the ground, and failure to use secondary containment, violations of 78a.54, 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(i)5iD, SWMA 301, 91.34(a), and 78a64a(b) are being issued.

The cause of the release was that a hose back pressured, biocide flowed back to the tank, and the tank overflowed. It was estimated that 10 gallons spilled.SPSI had not began remediation and was not on the pad when I arrived. No personal were on the pad upon my arrival.The following was observed:The contaminated area was adjacent to the gas production units (GPUs). It was unknown if any production fluid was present in addition to the biocide spilled; no elevated conductivity was observed. No remediation had begun and SPSI was not on the pad when I arrived on the pad. SPSI arrived to the site after the Department (Photo 1). An extremely strong odor was experienced on site in the vicinity of the contaminated area.SPSI then arrived on the pad and had not begun remediation while I was on site. The impacted area was located between the well heads and the GPUs. The impacted area appeared wet with small sections of pooled fluid (Photos 2-5).I asked SPSI if they had the SDS, and they did not. The SDS was not located on site with the site documents in the mailboxes. I was able to locate a Control and Disposal Plan and the Site Specific Safety and Environmental Plan and Policy. Comments: On 11/01/2024 a Complaint Inspection was conducted at the Folly Hollow Farm Unit OG Well Pad in response to a suspected release reported by multiple landowners. PA DEP Oil and Gas Inspector Supervisor Scott Sabocheck and Range Resources Representatives, Barry Bugbee and Nick Reda were on site at the time of inspection.Conductivity probe calibrated on 11/01/2024.The following was observed during the inspection:-An area of staining was observed beneath a flare stack located off secondary containment. Mr. Bugbee indicated that fluid was released, in a mist, from the flare stack yesterday(10/31/24) between 8:30 and 9:00 am, that the quantity released was approximately 2 gallons, and that the impacted material, except for the portion beneath the flare stack, was removed immediately after the release. The area of removed material and stained material combined appeared to be approximately 10 ft long by 10 ft wide in an irregular shape. The Department requests clarification on how the quantity released was determined (Photo 1).-Field conductivity screening was conducted within the area of stained material around and beneath the flare stack. Field conductivity readings were observed to be between 3.74 and 11.01 ms/cm (Photos 2-4).-Fluid was actively being released onto secondary containment during the plug removal from the well associated with the American Petroleum Institute (API) number 125-29107. Range Resources representative stated that the fluid released was fresh water (Photos 5-6).-Field conductivity screening was conducted within the area of fluid located in secondary containment. Field conductivity readings were observed to be between 5.41 ms/cm and Over Range (OR), which equates to greater than 20 ms/cm (Photos 7-9).-During the inspection, the flare stack was broken down and removed and the impacted material was excavated. The pad aggregate was removed to a depth of approximately 1-3 inches. The final area of removed material measured approximately 10 ft long by 10 ft wide (Photos 10-11).-Post-remediation field conductivity screening was conducted. Field conductivity readings were observed to be between 0.8 and 35.5 s/cm (Photos 12-15). Determination:Because the impacted material was removed and post-remediation screening values were below standard, violations of 78.57(a), 78a54, and SWMA 301 are being issued and immediately corrected.

At that time, crews were removing containment and other equipment associated with drilling activities that had just ended. I returned on December 23, 2016, to collect samples of the pad material for analysis of Oil and Grease and Total Petroleum Hydrocarbons (O&G TPH). These site visits are documented in Inspection Report No. 2547293. Chief excavated and removed the material from the affected area of the pad between December 23 and 27, 2016. Additionally, the release was in violation of 25 Pa. Code § 78a.54, which requires operators to control and dispose of drilling fluids and oil, among other things, in a manner that prevents pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth. Comments: Responded to an oil spill at this gas well location. The plug for the heater tube in the stock tank failed and allowed oil to leak out of the tank and into the diking. With the recent heavy rains, it appears the fluid in the diking overflowed through an open freshwater drain pipe and an inadequate diking height in spots. There was a ditch located on the backside of the diking where some of the oil flowed into but most of the oil appears to have gone out the freshwater drain pipe and then down the lease road. The lease road was approximately 55 yards long and pockets of oil were located throughout it and then into the weeds heading towards that same ditch that runs parallel to the lease road. The ditch empties into the Lake Wilhelm Road ditch. This Lake Wilhelm Road ditch just had a sheen of oil of oil on it west of the driveway. The last spot oil was seen in this ditch was about 10 yards east of the driveway culvert pipe outfall. No oil or sheen was seen emptying into or in the main stream of Calvin Clark Run itself. The oil was mostly contained with sorbent pads and by the grass and brush in the ditch. Based on site observations, it appears that less than 1 bbl of oil was released outside the diking area. With the heavy rains predicted again in the next 2 days, it was suggested for them to install a siphon dam in the field ditch right before it enters into the road ditch. A small excavator arrived on site and was in the process of doing this when I left. They were getting a vac truck out there today to remove all the fluid in the tank to stop the leaking of the oil. At 3:31 PM, Matt Kleese from Diamond Energy called me. He reported that they had just removed around 50 bbls of old motor oil from that stock tank. He said this well produces very little fluid and it was definitely old oil (he thinks motor oil). So he feels somebody had apparently dumped old motor oil in this tank. He said that he is probably going to file a police report on this incident.

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-06-26
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of Repsol's Bellows L (03-078) Well site in Columbia Twp, Bradford County on 6/26/2019 at 1130 hours. The weather was 79 degrees and mostly sunny. The inspection was conducted in response to a notice of the release called into the regional office. Kris Perritt (Repsol), Matt Bryan (Repsol), Andy Senefelder (Golder), and others from Repsol and numerous Bishop Brother's employees were all onsite. It was discovered that when the truck drivers were offloading the production tanks they were also taking water from the frac tank to top of their tanks. The tank was too low so when they would collect from the frac tank they were using the man-hole cover on the side of the tank to place hose through there to collect. This was reported to not have been properly closed. When the tank filled back up, production water was released from the cover. Upon this release, it was also discovered that the secondary containment around the frac tank had failed allowing most of the fluid within to be released to the pad surface. A reported 2 barrels was released. The release flowed into existing stormwater that had collected on the surface. In the area closest to the containment, I was obtaining readings of Over ranged on my PCSTestr35. Over Range represents a greater than 19.99ms/cm field reading. In the areas furthest from the release it was still clear that mixing had occurred and field readings of ~4.0-5.0ms/cm were still obtained. Repsol emptied the tank, removed it from the containment and marked the large area for excavation of 1-2 inches below the surface. Two vac trucks were deployed onsite to remove impacted waters. Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of Repsol's Bellows L (03-078) Well site in Columbia Twp, Bradford County on 6/26/2019 at 1130 hours. The weather was 79 degrees and mostly sunny. The inspection was conducted in response to a notice of the release called into the regional office. Kris Perritt (Repsol), Matt Bryan (Repsol), Andy Senefelder (Golder), and others from Repsol and numerous Bishop Brother's employees were all onsite. It was discovered that when the truck drivers were offloading the production tanks they were also taking water from the frac tank to top of their tanks. The tank was too low so when they would collect from the frac tank they were using the man-hole cover on the side of the tank to place hose through there to collect. This was reported to not have been properly closed. When the tank filled back up, production water was released from the cover. Upon this release, it was also discovered that the secondary containment around the frac tank had failed allowing most of the fluid within to be released to the pad surface. A reported 2 barrels was released. The release flowed into existing stormwater that had collected on the surface. In the area closest to the containment, I was obtaining readings of Over ranged on my PCSTestr35. Over Range represents a greater than 19.99ms/cm field reading. In the areas furthest from the release it was still clear that mixing had occurred and field readings of ~4.0-5.0ms/cm were still obtained. Permit API: 003-22235
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/05/2025
Comments: On March 5, 2025, the Department conducted an inspection at the Oliver East well pad in Forward Township, Allegheny County. This inspection was conducted to follow up to IR 3913651. IR 3913651 was conducted in response to the 1/29/2025 dumpline failure which reportedly released 5-10 gallons of produced water to the surface of the well pad. Notice of Termination request was approved by the Department for this site on November 10, 2022.The following was observed:The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is onsite (see photo 21). The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 22). The well pad appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photos 1). Sediment from the access road appears to threaten a stormwater drain along Williamsport Road (see photo 23). Although no sediment was observed inside this stormwater drain at the time of inspection, a layer of sediment was observed on debris that had accumulated on top of the storm drain grate.The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 3). Well 4H is equipped with a well tag with no evidence of fluid leaks to the ground around it, and it appears to be equipped for production (see photos 5 and 6). There are fourteen additional well heads onsite that also appear to be in production (see photo 4). An additional storage tank placed within secondary containment was observed onsite (see photo 7). This secondary containment appears to be holding a significant amount of rainwater at the time of inspection. Old GPU units are not equipped with secondary containment (see photo 9). However, their associated wells were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. New GPU units onsite are equipped with secondary containment (see photo 8).A reported absorbent material has been applied to the majority of the area impacted by the 1/29/2025 dumpline failure (see photos 10-12). The conductivity of the soil underneath this reported absorbent material remains significantly higher than the surrounding soil (see photos 13-20). Violation ID: 872386
Permit API: 059-24428
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Cumberland Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-12-23
Comments: On 12/19/19 a malfunction with the GPU occurred, causing the vessel to explode. On 12/20/19 OGI Joel Keller conducted inspection 2974755 and noted soil staining and a damp appearance. OGI Keller requested a follow up inspection be conducted by a WQS. On 12/23/19 at approximately 0800 I conducted a follow up inspection. The temperature was well below freezing at the time of inspection. Upon arriving at the explosion location I observed water on the access road that was not frozen, despite the freezing temperature. A soil conductivity probe was utilized and a reading od 12.02mS was observed (see photograph). Additional elevated soil conductivity readings were observed throughout the access road and on the east side of the access road. Trees and shrubs on the east side of the access road appeared wet. The liquid was not frozen and appeared to be brine, as further demonstrated by elevated soil conductivity readings in the area. No other trees or shrubs appeared wet, except for those east of the GPU location where elevated soil conductivity was observed. Additional elevated soil conductivity readings were observed further North toward the well head on the east side of the access road (see photographs). Elevated soil conductivity readings were also observed adjacent to brine tank 2. The highest reading observed was 12.83mS. Both brine tanks were severely corroded and brine tank 2 exhibited a large hole (see photographs). Brine tank 1 exhibited several smaller holes that appeared to have occurred due to shrapnel from the GPU explosion. The gravel in the former GPU location appeared to be stained, but the soil conductivity was not elevated. The Department recommends the visually impacted material is removed. Soil sample 3402-076 was collected from an area exhibiting elevated soil conductivity. Soil sample 3402-077 was collected from an area on the northwest portion of the site in an area that appeared to be unimpaired with low notably lower soil conductivity (see photographs). The Department recommends the spill is addressed consistent with the Act 2 process.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Pressure Build Up Tests (PBUTs) being performed on all (5) wells on the Hunter pad., the Hunter 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H. These PBUTs are being performed to assess the recent remedial work, CET (Casing Expansion Tool), deployment performed on all (5) Hunter wells production casing strings. This is the 3rd post CET deployment PBUTs being performed on these wells. - All (5) wells on the pad are in production. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a production tank via 2" common vent line. Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions on the well pad after a release was discovered by the Department on the pad surface on 3/20/2024. I met with Repsol representative Harry Lammy at the beginning of this inspection. The plugging rig is still in operation on the well pad. Six wells are staged for production. Multiple GPUs are present on the well pad and appear to be in good condition.A half-round tank is present on secondary containment in the area of the well pad impacted by the release which was discovered by the Department on 3/20/24. Along the south and west edge of this containment, several puddles of fluid were present which had an electrical conductivity between 2.54 mS/cm to 7.39 mS/cm. The Department recommends vacuuming up this fluid. According to Mr. Lammy, excavation of the impacted area of the pad surface has not yet taken place. He said that excavation would take place after the plugging rig has been moved off of the well pad on 4/11/24. In the NOV response provided to the Department via email on 4/11/24 by Andrew Senefelder of Repsol, Mr. Senefelder states that the elevated electrical conductivity fluid discovered on the pad surface by the Department on 3/20/24 was vacuumed up on the same day. The NOV response also states that Repsol intends to remediate the release in accordance with Act 2 remediation standards.Violations remain outstanding against permit 117-21545

Comments: On March 21, 2025, the Department conducted a follow up Inspection of the RWS Development 001 Well in response to an incident which is documented in IR 3941481 and 3941519 where violations were issued for a brine release.At the time of the inspection the well site appeared unchanged from the Department's previous inspection on 3/20/2025.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed charred vegetation on a slope adjacent to the well site, no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it, and no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead. Other production equipment was observed on site and appeared to be charred, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near any of this production equipment. A production tank was observed on site with a large hole in its side, the tank had approximately 1-2 in of fluid pooled at the bottom of it, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this production tank.A soil conductivity reading was taken directly under the hole in the tank with a reading of 10.16mS. The Department observed standing fluid in the ditch/channel in several locations. The Department observed 2 booms installed in the ditch. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid in the ditch in several locations with readings of 10.43mS, 7.28mS, 1.27mS, 0.93mS, 0.68mS, 0.78mS. The conductivity readings appeared to decrease with distance from the well/production tank. No standing fluid was observed in the ditch in approximately the last 45 feet prior to terminating near the stream. There did not appear to be a recent flow path of fluid in the section of ditch from the last location of standing water to the remainder of ditch before the stream. Conductivity readings were taken in this area of the ditch with readings of 0.53mS, 0.38mS, and 0.46mS.A conductivity reading was taken upstream of where the ditch appears to terminate with a reading of 0.67mS. A conductivity reading was then taken in the stream in the area where the ditch appears to terminate prior to the stream with a reading of 0.76mS. No sheen, discoloration, or foaming was observed in the stream.Based on the Department's observations and conductivity readings obtained, it appears that the conductivity readings are comparable to the previous inspections in regards to distance and levels of elevated readings in the ditch. It appears that released fluids may have been contained to the portions of the ditch where standing fluid was observed, and it did not appear from the observations and readings that there was a release into Waters of the Commonwealth.Prior to leaving the site, the Department called operator representative Ben Dickun to inquire when remediation was going to begin. Mr. Dickun stated they have contacted their consultant (Moody) and that work to remediate as well as a site assessment/sampling by Moody was scheduled to occur on Tuesday, 3/25/2025. The Department recommended during the call that immediate measures are properly implemented to commence remediation in response to the brine release that occurred onsite during the 3/19/2025 incident to prevent further migration of the onsite pollution and prevent pollution into WOC.Based on today's inspection, violations issued during IR 3941481 and 3941519 shall remain outstanding.

Comments: On March 21, 2025, the Department conducted a follow up Inspection of the RWS Development 001 Well in response to an incident which is documented in IR 3941481 and 3941519 where violations were issued for a brine release.At the time of the inspection the well site appeared unchanged from the Department's previous inspection on 3/20/2025.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed charred vegetation on a slope adjacent to the well site, no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it, and no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead. Other production equipment was observed on site and appeared to be charred, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near any of this production equipment. A production tank was observed on site with a large hole in its side, the tank had approximately 1-2 in of fluid pooled at the bottom of it, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this production tank.A soil conductivity reading was taken directly under the hole in the tank with a reading of 10.16mS. The Department observed standing fluid in the ditch/channel in several locations. The Department observed 2 booms installed in the ditch. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid in the ditch in several locations with readings of 10.43mS, 7.28mS, 1.27mS, 0.93mS, 0.68mS, 0.78mS. The conductivity readings appeared to decrease with distance from the well/production tank. No standing fluid was observed in the ditch in approximately the last 45 feet prior to terminating near the stream. There did not appear to be a recent flow path of fluid in the section of ditch from the last location of standing water to the remainder of ditch before the stream. Conductivity readings were taken in this area of the ditch with readings of 0.53mS, 0.38mS, and 0.46mS.A conductivity reading was taken upstream of where the ditch appears to terminate with a reading of 0.67mS. A conductivity reading was then taken in the stream in the area where the ditch appears to terminate prior to the stream with a reading of 0.76mS. No sheen, discoloration, or foaming was observed in the stream.Based on the Department's observations and conductivity readings obtained, it appears that the conductivity readings are comparable to the previous inspections in regards to distance and levels of elevated readings in the ditch. It appears that released fluids may have been contained to the portions of the ditch where standing fluid was observed, and it did not appear from the observations and readings that there was a release into Waters of the Commonwealth.Prior to leaving the site, the Department called operator representative Ben Dickun to inquire when remediation was going to begin. Mr. Dickun stated they have contacted their consultant (Moody) and that work to remediate as well as a site assessment/sampling by Moody was scheduled to occur on Tuesday, 3/25/2025. The Department recommended during the call that immediate measures are properly implemented to commence remediation in response to the brine release that occurred onsite during the 3/19/2025 incident to prevent further migration of the onsite pollution and prevent pollution into WOC.Based on today's inspection, violations issued during IR 3941481 and 3941519 shall remain outstanding.

Further inspections will be conducted to document ongoing remedation efforts, as well as confirmatory sampling to show that the remediation is sufficient.

Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. Onsite with DEP staff Alicia Furey and Lucas Eichner to collect a water sample from the earthen dike. The earthen dike is retaining fluid inside the bottom of the entire dike. There is approximately 4-5" of oily water pooled inside the dike. The dike drain remains closed and plugged. Water flowing into a separator barrel on top of a steel oil tank could be heard from the ground.Prior to the site visit water samples of the Bellows Spring was collected for analysis. There are 4 separate pipes flowing water into the cistern for the spring. Each pipe was identified, labeled, and sampled separately.After collecting samples from the earthen dike, DEP staff walked the hillside between the tank battery and Bellows Spring. The goal was to investigate any other oil and gas activity that may be located above the spring and that would be a potential contributor to the impact of the Bellows Spring. There was nothing observed between the tank battery and the Bellows Spring relating to oil and gas activity.At 2:05pm Mr. Rhoades was called via phone by the Department. The current condition of the tank battery was discussed with Mr. Rhoades and he indicated that a water truck is scheduled for next week to empty the dike and the brine tanks. Mr. Rhoades also stated that he has hired Moody and Associates as a consultant and that a check was in the mail to obtain their services. The Department clearly communicated the importance and urgency of starting the cleanup process at the site including the earthen dike area. Mr. Rhoades seemed to understand and asked if the water was good to drink yet in Reno and if individual households are being tested. I explained to Mr. Rhoades that samples have been taken from the spring by Oil and Gas Operations and that I was unaware of any other sampling/testing. It was also stated that the "Do not Consume" advisory has not yet been lifted from my knowledge at the time. The phone call was concluded with Mr. Rhoades indicating that he is starting the process to clean things up.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/30/2025
Violation Code: 78a91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under § 3221 of the 2012 Oil & Gas Act, 25 Pa. Code §§ 78a.92—78a.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID: 8250580
Permit API: 117-20767
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Union Township
Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 9/30/2025
Comments: At time of inspection: On site for a post-plugging inspection of the Heuer 1V (117-20767) well to check for gas at a plugged well. Met with Repsol rep. Bill Watts. There was water 2.5' below grade in the cellar with intermittent bubbling noticed. There was approximately 1 to 2 bubbles every 2 minutes. There was no gas detected with an Altair 5x gas meter. We waited for a water truck to vac out the water in the cellar. There was mud at the bottom of the cellar, the bubbling didn't increase. All vents and production casing were open and vented. The well-bore was full of water and there was no bubbling noticed. A Remote Methane Leak Detector (RMLD) was used to check the ambient air at the well for methane. An Altair 5x gas meter was used for further confirmation. There was no gas detected at the plugged well. There were no obvious concerns noticed. There is an outstanding 78a91(a) violation on this well that appears to have been addressed through extensive re-plugging operations performed from 7/11/2024 through 8/25/2025. The violation will be closed upon receipt of the plugging certificate. Operator may proceed with installation of monument/vent marker. Please include a picture of installed monument/vent marker, prior to burial, and an as plugged wellbore schematic with the submission of the Certificate of Well Plugging for this well.
